newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Fed Vice Chair Martin -- rate hike by July FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Fed Vice Chair Martin -- rate hike by July FOMC.

text.p: The Federal Reserve will likely raise its target for the overnight federal funds rate at either of its next two policy-making meetings, possibly by as much as 50 basis points, said former Fed Vice Chairman Preston Martin.

"If the economic data coming out continue to show substantial strength, I think (the Fed) will go right ahead and raise rates and it could even be 50 basis points this time," Martin told Reuters during a conference at the Jerome Levy Economics Institute here.

The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) next meets to chart interest rate policy on May 20 and then again on July 1 and 2. At its most recent meeting on March 25, the panel voted to raise the federal funds rate to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.
Martin said he sees 6.0 percent as a likely near-term ceiling for the funds rate.
"My surmise would be that (6.0 percent) would be adequate for some period of time," Martin said.
Should the FOMC opt for a move to 6.0 percent, Martin said he would expect some statement accompanying that action which would indicate that further rate hikes were not likely in the near future.
"That would be an appropriate public policy move," Martin said.
Martin cited Friday's report showing February retail sales grew by a revised 1.5 percent, sharply higher than the previously reported 0.8 percent gain, as a sign of the economy's vigor.
"It is one more signal, following several other signals, that the Fed should continue to raise rates," Martin added.
